facts.text: The eight machine-motion and brake-timing questions did not address functional safety and integrity level.
facts.quote:
Issues the eight questions did not ask about:

**Functional safety and integrity level.**

facts.text: An automatic brake is a safety function under the ISO 19014 series and ISO 13849, with ISO 21448 addressing perception limits; the cited evidence is draft.
facts.quote: An automatic brake is a safety function under the ISO 19014 series and ISO 13849, with ISO 21448 for perception limits.

facts.text: The required performance level for an automatic brake drives architecture and validation effort as much as threshold tuning does; the cited evidence is draft.
facts.quote: The required performance level drives architecture and validation effort as much as threshold tuning does.

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2 places the collision-avoidance device outside the machine controller and states that the device is not plug-and-play; the cited evidence is draft.
facts.quote: ISO/TS 21815-2 places the collision-avoidance device outside the machine controller and states that it is not plug-and-play.

facts.text: Perception performance may dominate braking-model accuracy, an issue not addressed by the eight machine-motion and brake-timing questions.
facts.quote: **Perception performance may dominate braking-model accuracy.**

facts.text: ISO's distance budget starts at detection.
facts.quote: ISO's distance budget starts at detection.

facts.text: If dust, fog, darkness, glare, mud on a sensor, self-occlusion, vibration or poor mounting reduce reliable detection range below required stopping distance, no brake model can recover the lost margin.
facts.quote: If dust, fog, darkness, glare, mud on a sensor, self-occlusion, vibration or poor mounting cut reliable detection range below the required stopping distance, no brake model can recover the lost margin.

facts.text: Sensor position and machine geometry need a geometric model rather than just recalibration, an issue omitted from the eight machine-motion and brake-timing questions.
facts.quote: **Sensor position and machine geometry need a geometric model, not just recalibration.**

facts.text: Different machine lengths, widths, articulation centers, body structures and blind zones alter both detection coverage and the collision envelope; a transferable system needs machine geometry as configuration data.
facts.quote: Different lengths, widths, articulation centers, body structures and blind zones alter both detection coverage and the collision envelope; a transferable system needs machine geometry as configuration data.

facts.text: Buckets, forks, blades, booms, dump bodies and trailers change swept volume and center of gravity, an attachment-geometry issue omitted from the eight questions.
facts.quote: **Attachments and changing geometry.** Buckets, forks, blades, booms, dump bodies and trailers change swept volume and center of gravity.

facts.text: ISO 21815-4's 2026 scope has limitations related to machine and tool height, so the collision standard does not cover every attachment hazard; the cited evidence is draft.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-4's 2026 scope has limitations related to machine and tool height, so not every attachment hazard is covered by the collision standard.

facts.text: Braking policy should not treat a person, another haul truck, a cone, a berm, a rock pile and vegetation identically because false-positive costs and required clearances differ.
facts.quote: Braking policy should not treat a person, another haul truck, a cone, a berm, a rock pile and vegetation identically; the false-positive cost and required clearance differ

facts.text: Permissible object-class semantics for braking policy need safety requirements before threshold tuning begins.
facts.quote: the permissible semantics need safety requirements before threshold tuning begins.

facts.text: Avoiding the nearest detected object can create a second conflict, especially during steering or articulation; a scalar nearest-range trigger is inadequate in crowded work zones.
facts.quote: Avoiding the nearest detected object can create a second conflict, especially during steering or articulation; a scalar nearest-range trigger is inadequate in crowded work zones.

facts.text: Brake fade, wear, faults and stored-energy state were omitted from the eight machine-motion and brake-timing questions.
facts.quote: **Brake fade, wear, faults and stored-energy state.**

facts.text: Heat, wear and accumulator charge change braking deceleration and latency over a shift.
facts.quote: Heat, wear and accumulator charge change deceleration and latency over a shift

facts.text: NIOSH's roadmap found fatal accidents in which vehicles failed to stop despite some combination of brakes being available.
facts.quote: NIOSH's roadmap found fatal accidents where vehicles failed to stop "despite there being some combination of brakes available".

facts.text: ISO 3450 includes service-brake, secondary-brake and stored-energy provisions.
facts.quote: ISO 3450 includes service, secondary and stored-energy provisions

facts.text: An automatic braking system should not assume nominal service-brake performance after detected degradation.

facts.text: Operators may come to rely on the automatic braking system through risk compensation, a human-factors issue omitted from the eight questions.
